established: The CLI process reached a valid init; an unconditional .cmd spawn/quoting failure cannot explain this particular captured session.

AgentChatSession records input before writing or flushing stdin. No input was captured, and no capture-error marker was present. Evidence points to the host pre-write path, not CLI processing of an accepted user prompt.
The IDE bridge ACL operation independently timed out after 30 seconds. The log does not show a corresponding chat draft failure.

The driver waits for a protocol terminal after backgrounding the task tab and does not capture original-tab state on failure; a host-side delivery rejection can therefore consume the remaining 20-minute harness deadline without a CLI terminal.
The 15-second permission acknowledgement timer changes display status/reason only. It does not change revision/generation, reject input capability, or prevent a late valid init acknowledgement.
notEstablished: 133.289 seconds from driver submit to init is not the awaitReady duration: beginSend, configuration read, binary resolution and session startup precede the 120-second capability wait, and their completion timestamps are absent.
No evidence proves that optional task worklog caused the block. The native wrapper disabling it is not a verified Windows fix.
No evidence proves that the bridge ACL timeout also blocked draft preparation. ChatDraftStore storage and bridge lockfile paths are separate.

The exact pre-write blocker cannot be selected from current records: cancelled init wait, capability callback failure, draft preparation/status persistence failure, changed/disposed generation, or delayed EDT reservation remain possible.

lowRiskHarnessRecommendationsOnly: On failure, preserve a bounded original-tab UI snapshot (existing snapshot fields include editable, sendInFlight, receiptReady, childRunning, draftStatus and transcript status text). Keep collection best-effort so its own deadline does not replace the original error.
Observe definitive host delivery error text and save it separately from the raw CLI protocol; do not fabricate a CLI terminal or input ACK.

Optionally capture bounded Java thread names/stacks while the send worker is waiting, plus timestamps for initialization/receipt readiness. No resend, synthetic prompt, permission bypass, or published plugin replacement.
Keep the public plugin and current running jobs unchanged; inspect their archived input/ACK/UI chronology before proposing any readiness fix.
